turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student, and I have that page printed in my bag.

So what else do you have, Hale, or is that it?
I don't need more proof than that.

"I don't need more proof." I'm writing that down.

Your own procedure, section 4.3, says detection software doesn't establish a concern by itself. Check it.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.

"Some people." Who, exactly? My child never lies, and I'm not going to sit here while you imply it.

Are you calling me a liar too?

Then I'll be in the principal's office when we're done here. Before I go, I'm asking you on the record: did anyone call me before that zero went into the gradebook? Section 4.2 says someone should have.
